correctness.rationale: Exact Fock monomial radial diagonalization yields gamma-weighted mask moments. Fourier coefficients of a periodic single arc are explicit; the first nonzero harmonics have modulus \(r\) strictly exceeding all higher harmonics. Their two-by-two Hankel minor is exactly \(H_n=-4|b|^2\sin^2(\theta)r^{2n+4}\) at principal order. The remainder is exponentially smaller, hence eventual negativity and geometric convergence of ratios. Two normalized consecutive deviations determine the complex Fourier coefficient because \(\sin\theta>0\), and \(0<\rho<1\) guarantees \(b\ne0\). Wrapped and unwrapped arcs are included. The supplementary checker passed 58 assertions; none substitutes for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural 3-parameter spectral inverse problem for periodic radial Gaussian observation geometry is resolved quantitatively. Oscillations can mask the leading harmonic and make naive log ratios undefined or unstable, whereas a sign-definite adjacent Hankel determinant robustly reveals the decay scale independently of the unknown phase; the residual complex recurrence recovers the geometric origin. This is motivated by localization calibration and provides exact structural asymptotics beyond abstract radial-symbol identifiability. The result is not a finite-noise stability theorem.
